# Independent audit: unbuffered smoothing and optimization over active menus

PASS for the stated attained minimal-bad-class interface in
`candidate 6e754f2bf13bdbd1`,
and for the full-menu directional duality and quantifiers in
`candidate 26e4bc3a75ffef69`.
The sharp general numerical payment remains unproved.

## Smoothing without the energy buffer

The global inequality beta_h>=beta_0 follows from the OUTWARD threshold
average and is available before compactness. On the already proved
compact original bad-sublevel class, the uniform slab comparison is
independent of all base tilts and gives the stated O(h) error. This
orders the compactness argument correctly.

At epsilon=0, full normal stationarity gives

    m-A(0,Sigma u)=S Y  (Gamma(u)=1).

The active quantile is locally strictly decreasing, so a common active
cap at an integer convex combination of deepest marks is active at
every constituent. All of N,c,S,m,A are then identical. The displayed
identity forces equality of the FULL marks. This proves the unique own
mark as well as the parity separation, without an energy profile.

The important contact distinction is correctly retained. A frozen
balanced menu has sum rho u=0, so its affine contact vanishes on its
whole own fiber. Consequently arbitrary independent normal velocities
cannot be treated by the unique-contact H envelope. Keeping the normals
fixed instead leaves the exact threshold budget

    sum rho c_j(t,q)=sum rho a_j.p.

If all its through-point cap masses exceeded q, all thresholds would
strictly exceed their through-point values; summing gives a contradiction.
Thus this is an actual whole-fiber cover, including equality cases.

The covariance derivative is (D-J_j)/(2M), and differentiation of the
width contributes A_j times this derivative. Since the threshold
budget has derivative zero, the coarea-dual mixture of these losses
is the exact cover loss. Finite cone separation therefore gives

    Xi=W-beta + (sum omega(-A_j)[u_j.(X-g_z)]^2 + Abar)/(2M).

Every covariance coefficient is nonnegative. This argument uses no
unproved separate-source minimum and no signed-normal contact shortcut.
The optional log-width identity has the correct sign: the cap loss
under log h velocity s is A_j s, hence -Abar=M tau at an interior
minimum of beta_h-tau log h. Fixed-width stationarity does not require
that optional selection.

## All active menus

For a fixed source, the correct response weights are probabilities nu
with integral S_N(u-epsilon grad f) dnu=0. The raw quantile weights rho
are proportional to S_N dnu. Thus replacing raw balance by response
balance without the coareas would be wrong; the note does not do so.

The convex-hull proof of the directional duality is sound. If B is the
compact hull of (g_N,L_N), the optimized value is the highest point of
B over g=0. A strictly higher point can be separated with positive last
coordinate coefficient: compare it to the point of B over g=0 to see
that positivity directly. This yields a finite approximate mark velocity,
even when the minimizing velocity is not attained.

Caratheodory initially gives d+2 caps. A dependence preserving the first
d coordinates and total weight has zero last-coordinate variation by
maximality, so one weight can be removed. This proves the d+1 count.

The matching upper bound for the source derivative uses the exact finite
cover. For epsilon>0 its old contact is uniquely the source, as in the
H construction. At epsilon=0 the same derivative proof instead uses the
frozen-normal cover just audited, whose threshold budget is constant.
For the lower bound, any fixed finite trial mark velocity suffices, so
no unproved O(t) control on the maximizing mark is needed.

Actual minimality consequently implies, for every physical field Phi,

    min_i max_(nu in M_i) [integral L_i,N(Phi)dnu-beta D] <= 0.

The independent menu maxima are attained; this is equivalent to the
failure of a simultaneous strict descent for EVERY complete selection
of one menu per source. Each such selection has a coherent source
separator valid for all fields. Its source weights may depend on the
selection. The exact two-interval scalar example proves that no universal
menu-independent source separator follows just from these quantifiers.

The sufficient exposed-target criterion is therefore legitimate, but
the existence of such favorable target menus for arbitrary sources is
not implied. The central triangle example illustrates the distinction:
one valid menu fails an individual Gamma payment while another actual
menu supplies a real descent. It does not establish the general
best-active-menu efficiency lemma.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
